competency_fulfillment.rationale: The items comprehensively fulfill all requirements of the MATATAG learning competency across multiple representations. Concrete and pictorial array/grouping models are represented in "Shade 20 squares into 4 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?" (seed 55) and "This array has 90 squares split into 10 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?" (seed 101). Equal sharing is directly evaluated in "Moses wants to share 90 baskets equally among 10 friends. How many baskets does each friend get?" (seed 601). Repeated subtraction is modeled in "Start with 80. Subtract 10 repeatedly until reaching 0: you subtract ___ times." (seed 44). Division expressions with numerals are tested in "What is 2 ÷ 2?" (seed 42) and "90 ÷ 10 = ___" (seed 603).

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Every conceptual facet described in the competency is covered across the sample set. Equal sharing in context is covered by "Moses wants to share 90 baskets equally among 10 friends. How many baskets does each friend get?" (seed 601). Equal grouping and row array structures are assessed in "Shade 20 squares into 4 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?" (seed 55) and "This array has 90 squares split into 10 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?" (seed 101). Repeated subtraction conceptualization is assessed in "Start with 90. Subtract 10 repeatedly until reaching 0: you subtract ___ times." (seed 501) and "Starting from 15 and subtracting 5 repeatedly, you subtract 75 times before reaching 0. True or False?" (seed 50). Numerical fact equations are covered in "What is 20 ÷ 10?" (seed 46) and "What is 20 ÷ 5?" (seed 43).

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language and conceptual complexity are completely appropriate for Grade 2 Quarter 3 students. Sentences are concise and clear, such as "What is 40 ÷ 10?" (seed 45) and "Moses wants to share 90 baskets equally among 10 friends. How many baskets does each friend get?" (seed 601). Error analysis items such as error analysis (seed 51: "80 ÷ 10 = ___") (seed 51) and student error analysis (seed 500: "Starting from 90 and subtracting 10 repeatedly, you subtract ___ times before reaching 0") (seed 500) target common student misconceptions (such as subtracting once instead of finding the quotient) without unnecessary linguistic complexity.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The items use a wide range of question formatters to test division mastery from multiple angles. Formatters include mcq ("What is 80 ÷ 10?", seed 502; "What is 15 ÷ 3?", seed 602), cloze ("90 ÷ 10 = ___", seed 603; "Start with 80. Subtract 10 repeatedly until reaching 0: you subtract ___ times.", seed 44), true_false ("Starting from 15 and subtracting 5 repeatedly, you subtract 75 times before reaching 0. True or False?", seed 50), set_fill_in_blank ("Shade 20 squares into 4 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", seed 55), read_mcq ("This array has 90 squares split into 10 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", seed 101), and error_detect (error analysis (seed 51: "80 ÷ 10 = ___"), seed 51).

competency_alignment.rationale: All questions align directly to the competency and do not drift into out-of-scope domains (such as remainders or 2-digit divisors outside of basic multiples of 10). Every item focuses on concrete/pictorial grouping, repeated subtraction, or basic division facts, as seen in "What is 10 ÷ 10?" (seed 600), "What is 20 ÷ 4?" (seed 604), and "Start with 90. Subtract 10 repeatedly until reaching 0: you subtract ___ times." (seed 501).

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Number scales are fully calibrated to Grade 2 division standards. Dividends range from small single/double digits (e.g. 2 in "What is 2 ÷ 2?", seed 42; 15 in "What is 15 ÷ 3?", seed 602; 20 in "What is 20 ÷ 4?", seed 604) up to 90 (e.g., "Start with 90. Subtract 10 repeatedly until reaching 0: you subtract ___ times.", seed 501; "This array has 90 squares split into 10 equal rows. How many squares are in each row?", seed 101) with divisors 2, 3, 4, 5, and 10 and exact integer quotients, perfectly respecting Grade 2 computation scope.
